# Upcoming SaladCloud Price Changes: September 12, 2026

SaladCloud GPU and vCPU pricing is changing on September 12, 2026: 15 GPU classes drop 25% on average, while RTX 5090 and 4090 prices increase.

Jared Carpenter

Product Update SaladCloud Tue Sep 01 2026

We're updating GPU and vCPU pricing on SaladCloud to correct places where our prices had drifted out of line with demand: some classes were priced above what the market will bear, and a couple were priced below it.

These changes take effect Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 00:00 UTC, and they will impact active and running instances at that time.

## Summary Copy Anchor Link

- Prices for 15 GPU classes are coming down, by 25% on average at High Priority (individual classes fall between 16% and 38%).
- Lowest Priority pricing is staying stable, with the exception of the RTX 5080, where it comes down from $0.180 to $0.150.
- RTX 5090 and RTX 4090: we've had to raise High, Medium, and Low Priority prices on these two classes. At High Priority, the RTX 5090 moves from $0.450 to $0.500 and the RTX 4090 from $0.300 to $0.330.
- For CPU-only workloads, vCPU pricing is going up from $0.004 to $0.005 per vCPU per hour. RAM pricing is unchanged. GPU container groups aren't charged for vCPU or RAM.
- Every GPU class not listed below is unchanged.

highlights:
# Earning Rate Changes: September 12

Salad earning rates change September 12, 2026: RTX 5090 and 4090 rates go up, 15 GPU classes come down at higher priority tiers, CPU payouts rise.

Jared Carpenter

Product Update SaladApp Fri Sep 04 2026

GPU prices will change on September 12th, 00:00 UTC. Before you worry, these changes include increased earnings for highly demanded GPUs, and almost all decreases are limited to specific priority tiers. See the chart below if you want to check what your future earning situation will look like. Keep reading for more context as to why we're altering our prices again.

If you're running a 5090 or a 4090, your rates are going up at High, Medium, and Low priority, since demand for those cards keeps outrunning what the network can supply. Fifteen other GPU classes are coming down, mostly at those same three tiers, while Lowest priority stays where it is on everything except the RTX 5080. CPU-only workloads are getting a raise too, covered below. And if your card isn't in the chart at all, nothing about your earnings is changing.

...

Payouts for CPU-only workloads are going from $0.0035 to $0.004 per hour per vCPU, which works out to a bit over 14% more for the exact same work.

results.title: SaladCloud Alternative (2026): GPU Prices vs PowerGPU
highlights:
SaladCloud runs containers on thousands of consumer PCs whose owners rent out idle GPUs. That makes it the cheapest RTX 4090 and 5090 by the hour, at the cost of node churn, no SSH, no persistent disks and residential-grade networking. Payment is by card; pricing is announced to change on 12 September 2026.

...

SaladCloud column: as published on salad.com on 2026-09-03. Details change — verify before you decide.

## SaladCloud vs PowerGPU prices, GPU by GPU

Public on-demand list prices per GPU-hour on SaladCloud's pricing page (2026-09-03) against PowerGPU's fixed rates today — every PowerGPU price is the public marketplace median × 0.70, rounded down, re-checked weekly.

| GPU | SaladCloud list | PowerGPU on-demand | PowerGPU interruptible | Difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 5090 consumer node, 32 GB | $0.25 | $0.481 | $0.240 | +92% on PowerGPU |
| RTX 4090 consumer node, 24 GB | $0.16 | $0.354 | $0.177 | +121% on PowerGPU |

Configurations differ (node sizes, tiers, regions); the note beside each card says which SaladCloud price is quoted. Negative differences mean SaladCloud is cheaper on that card.

...

## Why teams switch to PowerGPU

- Honest math: SaladCloud is cheaper per hour on the RTX 4090 ($0.16 vs our on-demand rate) — but PowerGPU interruptible capacity on the same card is priced below Salad's rate, on datacenter hardware.
- SSH, Jupyter, persistent volumes, full VMs and datacenter cards (H100, H200, L40S) — none of which exist on a residential node network.
- Deterministic hardware: the machine you deploy on is the machine you get, with a known CPU, RAM, disk and uplink.
- Crypto payments with no KYC.

results.title: Salad: Distributed GPUs from $0.02 an hour for inference
highlights: Every GPU class has four priority tiers: High is never preempted by other workloads, Medium and Low can be, and Lowest is the cheapest and the easiest to interrupt. Deployments above 100 GPUs, long-running jobs and committed spend get volume pricing from sales, and reserved RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell servers (Salad Dedicated) are quoted per contract. ... results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

H100: At $4.50, Nebius moves above Runpod ($3.49), Crusoe ($3.90) and Lambda ($4.29). It stays below CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance, about $6.16 per GPU.

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55). It stays below Together AI ($5.99) and CoreWeave (about $6.31 per GPU).

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

### What to do before October 1

Ask about locking today's rate. Ask Nebius whether a commitment signed before October 1 is priced at the current rate. Get the answer in writing, with the rate and term.

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses. A quote issued in September may still show the old price.

results.title: Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October By Investing.com
highlights:
© Reuters

Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.

results.title: Nebius Said to Raise Prices for its On-demand Compute Resources Starting October | MemoryMarket - memory prices, market analysis, industry news, research report
results.author: By: M
highlights: According to media reports, Nebius will raise prices for some of its on-demand computing resources starting October 1, marking the company's second round of price increases since May. Under the new pricing plan, the price of H100 will rise from $3.85 per GPU hour to $4.50, an increase of about 17%; H200 will rise 20% from $4.50 to $5.40; B200 will rise nearly 19% from $7.15 to $8.50; and B300 will rise about 21% from $7.85 per GPU hour to $9.50. The changes also extend to CPU-only compute. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates will rise 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour from $0.012, while Genoa memory will increase about 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032. The ultimate impact on customers' bills will therefore depend on their configurations and usage.
